**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal in sharedFaceRefusal))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal in sharedFaceRefusal))_

- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via endsWith (literal, a string literal in STRING_METHOD_OF), startsWith (literal, a string literal in STRING_METHOD_OF))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal in sharedFaceRefusal))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 31 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bd245620a6809a5a468dd693c3d761440d790173` — the merge of head `77060e6d067b0b114ee17b07079f7fe388592900` into base `1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bd245620a6809a5a468dd693c3d761440d790173 && git checkout bd245620a6809a5a468dd693c3d761440d790173
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a 77060e6d067b0b114ee17b07079f7fe388592900 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a && git merge --no-ff 77060e6d067b0b114ee17b07079f7fe388592900

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `77060e6d067b0b114ee17b07079f7fe388592900`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Scope, checked against the tree.** Delta vs merge-base `0bd11261` is exactly 3 files: the rule (`packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`), its test, one `@objectstack/lint` changeset. `git diff origin/main..77060e6d -- packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts` is empty: no runtime, compiler or shared-face source moves. `@objectstack/spec/data` is already a lint dependency (4 other lint files import it) and exports both faces (`data/index.ts:15,23`). CI at the head: 32 success / 6 skipped / 0 failing.
- **Type family (class 1): RIGHT.** Measured in a detached worktree at the head (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run` on the PR test file plus a review probe: 2 files, 126 passed, the PR's own 120 included). 16 spellings — `!=`/`==`/`!(==)` against `org_user_ids`/`positions`/`accessible_org_ids`, `in` against `id`/`email`/`organization_id` and its negation, `in current_user`, `startsWith`/`contains`/`endsWith(current_user)`, a string method on a membership key, and the SQL-bridge spellings `reviewer_id != current_user.org_user_ids`, `reviewer_id IN current_user.id`, `reviewer_id IN (current_user.id)`, `reviewer_id = current_user.positions` — each yields exactly one finding per clause: `rls-predicate-unenforceable` at `permissions[0].rowLevelSecurity[0].using` / `.check`, `using`/`check` parity holds, and every hint carries a pasteable CEL rewrite with the predicate's own field and key (e.g. `!(record.reviewer_id in current_user.org_user_ids)`, `record.reviewer_id == current_user.id`, the derived key menus for the bare root). Ground truth: `compileCelToFilter` with runtime-typed bindings refuses each (`\`in\` requires an array/list on the right`, `\`!=\` compares one value, but its comparand … resolves to a list`, `"startsWith()" argument must be a string literal`); `ExecutionContextSchema` fixes the types (`userId`/`tenantId`/`email` strings, `positions`/`org_user_ids`/`accessible_org_ids` string arrays) and `RLSCompiler.compileFilter` (`rls-compiler.ts:445-466`) binds exactly those keys, merging `rlsMembership` arrays only, so the refusal recurs on every request. The new `DROPPED_EVERY_REQUEST` text matches the runtime: `isSupportedRlsExpression` is true so the "uncompilable predicate" WARN branch (`:556`) is skipped, the policy joins `deniedBy`, and `warnFailClosedDenial` (`:613-640`) fires only when `filters.length === 0`. The existing `consequence()` default text is byte-identical.
- **Null family (class 2): RIGHT, with the truthful qualifier the message carries.** 7 shapes (`in ['open', null]`, `in [null]`, `!(in ['open', null])`, `> null`, `>= null`, `< null`, `<= null`) plus `in ['open', null] || owner_id == current_user.id` each give exactly one finding per clause under the same id; the message says the policy is NOT dropped, which is the measured runtime (#20212): my compiler probe confirms `in ['a', null]` lowers to `$in: ['a', null]` and `> null` to `$gt: null`, so the RLS data path executes them with SQL null semantics. The judge is the ruled contract, not a guess: `assertListComparandShapes` (null-member arm, null-ordering arm) and `normalizeFilterComparandTypes`, graded on `code === 'INVALID_FILTER'`; `service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts:7,687,890` runs the identical pair on every RLS read scope, so every analytics query over the object is refused. Is `error` at `os validate` truthful for a policy that "works"? Yes: `in ['open', null]` on SQL silently behaves as `in ['open']` (not as written), `!(… null)` hides every row while its own `check` admits the write, `in [null]` reads nothing on SQL and the null rows on memory/mongo. No policy that behaves as written on every backend is refused, and the card's direction (`5823840908`) asks for exactly this refusal. The rewrites are local and correct under an enclosing `!`: `!(status in ["open"] || status == null)` is "neither open nor missing".
- **False-positive hunt: none found.** 50 sources × 2 clauses, head identical to base and all clean: `record.owner_id == current_user.id` (CEL, bare, SQL `=`, and `!=`); `in` against every membership key and `!(in …)`; `current_user.email == 'lit'` and `!= 'lit'` alone, in `||` and beside a membership test; `== null` / `!= null` / `id == null`; literal lists of strings, numbers, booleans, the empty `[]` and its negation; ordering against numbers, strings, and scalar keys (`> current_user.id`); string methods with literals and scalar keys; nested `&&` / `||` / `!`; §7.3.1 app keys under `in` (`team_member_ids`, `territory_account_ids`); `1 == 1`; `true`; field-to-field. `record.f == current_user.nope` keeps `rls-predicate-unknown-user-variable`; `record.f.startsWith(current_user.team_member_ids)` keeps it too (app keys are arrays). The only 2 "hits" in my table are `field = null` → `rls-predicate-unknown-field` on base AND head — my synthetic stack does not declare a field named `field`.
- **Discriminator soundness: sound in the false-positive direction.** A predicate the runtime accepts compiles under the runtime-typed probe, so `refusal` is null and `attributeTypeFault` never runs. The one accepted class that IS refused under the probe — a value-dependent constant fold — needs two things no single swap gives it: the swapped compile must succeed AND the marker must land in a lowered field position. `SWAP_SCALAR` keeps the folds refused (probed: `current_user.id > '__objectstack_lint_probe__'` and `current_user.email != '__objectstack_lint_probe__'` both silent). Ablation A in the PR (2 red incl. the probe-artefact control) is consistent with what I read. The cost is in the other direction, all measured and all fail-closed at runtime: (a) two type faults in one predicate (`record.a in current_user.id && record.b in current_user.email`) → silent; (b) a type fault beside a value-dependent fold → silent; (c) ORDER dependence: `record.f in current_user.id || record.g in current_user.team_ids` → silent, while `record.g in current_user.team_ids || record.f in current_user.id` → reported (an app key discovered after the fault never gets bound, so no swap compiles); (d) `record.f == current_user.nope && record.g in current_user.id` → silent on base and head (the later fault masks the unknown-variable finding — pre-existing). (a), (b), (d) are in the docblock / Acceptance notes; (c) is not written down.
- **Census: reproduced at 0.** My own extraction at the head (`git grep` for quoted `using:` / `check:` literals over the whole tree; 303 predicates, 124 outside tests; `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` and the `packages/qa/dogfood` fixtures are in it; no unquoted YAML/JSON policy exists in the tree) run through the merge-base rule copy (blob `cb850a12` == `0bd11261`'s) and the head rule in one process: **0 changed, 0 newly flagged**. A direct grep for every flagged spelling (`(!=|==) current_user.SET`, `in current_user.SCALAR`, `in current_user` bare, string methods on the root or a set, `null` inside a list, ordering against `null`) finds 0 producers outside the changeset and the rule.
- **Reach and plumbing.** `runAuthoringRules('validate', …)` returns the finding at `error`; the rule is `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL` (`authoring-rules.ts:1831-1843`), and `validate.ts:377-414` exits 1 on any error — so `os validate` / `build` / `lint` now refuse these. Multi-policy paths and `where` are correct (`permissions[1].rowLevelSecurity[2].using`, `permission set "b" policy "q3" on object "crm_opportunity"`). A policy on an object the stack does not declare still gets the object-independent type/null findings. A disabled policy is still judged (the rule's documented design).

### ② Semver level

- Declared: `@objectstack/lint` **minor**, no BREAKING banner, PR body `Clause-②: no` (bare), no `Clause-②` line in the changeset body.
- **Gates, from the scripts at `origin/main` (not rerun):** `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — `minor` is not `major`; the level axis reads a bare `no` as `not-declared` and stands down. `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` — `breakingDeclaration()` signals are a `major` bump, `**BREAKING` / `BREAKING CHANGE`, a `!:` summary, or a `Clause-②` arm reading `narrowing`; this changeset carries none, so it is not judged. Both satisfied mechanically.
- **`minor` is right.** The exact precedent is on `main`, in this rule's own file: `.changeset/rls-predicate-references.md` (#16119) added two new `error` ids and states that a stack "built clean before and now fails `os validate`" — graded `minor`, no banner, bare declaration. The 2026-09-04 WHICH LEVEL ruling sets `minor` as the floor for a widening and never forbids it for a behaviour change; `patch` would be the under-grade for new gating findings.
- **Banner: acceptable, noted.** The repo also carries the opposite reading (`validate-refuses-blank-structural-condition.md`, lint CHANGELOG `8640fb2`: "BREAKING accept-set change on the `os validate` gating tier", banner + `adr-0087` marker). For the type family nothing narrows: the compiler already refuses every one of these, and the membership-set form is registered as `cel-predicate-list-comparand-refused` under protocol major 18 with its FROM→TO; `in` against a scalar or the root, and a string method on a non-string, were never accepted. For the null family the `os validate` refusal is new for a shape the RLS data path executes, and the changeset says so in bold with a FROM→TO per shape and the 0-flip census — the information a banner exists to carry. Under the #16119 precedent this is not blocking. The seat's ACCEPT prose "it narrows" beside the bare `Clause-②: no` is a wording tension only: the arm's single reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) gives a bare `no` the non-breaking reading, and no gate reads the prose.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **#20212 (filed, open, bare):** the RLS data path skips the shared comparand faces, so a null member / null bound reaches driver-sql and read vs `check` disagree. Consequence for this PR: on the null family the lint and the runtime data path now disagree BY DESIGN (lint refuses, runtime executes per backend); the lint agrees with the contract faces, the engine seam and analytics. The changeset's "refuses both in every filter it is sent" is true of the faces, not of the RLS path — the finding's message states the exception correctly.
- **`18.cel-predicate-list-comparand-refused.ts` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`):** "The authoring lint reports a list literal as rls-predicate-unenforceable; a membership set holds its value only per request, so that form is refused at request time" is now incomplete (the lint reports the membership-set form too). No pin test guards that sentence (grep). Carrier: none, as the dev recorded.
- **Ordering against a set or the root — unexercised, partly mis-messaged.** `record.f > current_user.positions` lowers to `{ f: { $gt: ['…'] } }`; the shape door checks ordering slots for `null` only and the type door keeps arrays, so the lint is silent and the runtime answer is unmeasured (dev's flag confirmed). `record.f > current_user` (root) lowers to `$gt: the whole context object` and IS reported through the face family — but `firstSentence(faced)` quotes the lint's probe into the author-facing message (`… is a plain object ({"id":"__objectstack_lint_probe__","org…), which no driver can compare`) and the null-specific `FACE_REFUSED_CONSEQUENCE` does not describe this shape; the hint falls back to the generic subset sentence. 0 producers in the tree. Non-blocking; a follow-up should redact the quoted comparand on a non-null face refusal.
- **Id documentation drift in the same file:** `RLS_PREDICATE_UNENFORCEABLE`'s JSDoc ("the policy enforces nothing", line 184) and the "three ids, and why not one" paragraph (lines 83–98) predate the null family, whose own message says the policy is NOT dropped. The #16119 block was updated for #19951; these two were not. Non-blocking.
- **Conservative misses (real per-request refusals that escape):** two type faults in one predicate; a fault beside a value-dependent fold; a fault after an undiscovered app key (order-dependent, not documented); an unknown key masked by a later fault (pre-existing). All fail closed at runtime; none is a false positive.
- **Hint spelling:** for a bare-identifier or SQL-bridge source the "replace `record.reviewer_id in current_user.id`" clause names the normalised CEL spelling rather than the author's literal text; the "with …" half is valid CEL the bridge accepts unchanged. Non-blocking.
- Nothing else: no export, wire shape or rule id is added; no test outside `packages/lint` asserts an `rls-predicate-*` id (grep: prose only in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts`).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19951-rls-lint-membership-key-silent`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Rjy9MeetSfq34PKn81CRiN`

**VERDICT: PASS**
